name: STAGE ROAD & COACH STOP
materialIdentity: cold indigo, grey and sky, with warm ochre and gold only where the lamp and the windows reach -- ruling 17a. The only night exterior in the game.
note: Doc 05 Room 1 plus doc 17 v2, with errata ruling 19a's canonical per-state line sets. Doc 17 note 3: THE ROAD EAST's LISTEN variants 2 and 3 are identical to each other AND to the line at the high ridge in Act IV -- three uses of 'Nothing coming', a hundred yards and fifteen hours apart. Do not vary them. THE COACH, THE TEAM and THE WATCHMAN'S LAMP are state-gated: the coach becomes THE ROAD WEST OUT once it has gone, the team exists only while it is here, and there is no lamp at all until Hob walks onto the road.

cycling.note: Doc 18: a carried flame in still air, not a torch. It is the brightest and only warm object in the frame and must not draw more attention than a lamp deserves. Four entries at the top of accent_gold, reserved -- which is also what now keeps the coach lantern and the clasp on Thad's case below it, a rule doc 17 stated and nothing was checking.

Doc 18: moonlight on standing water shifting as air moves over it, barely perceptible. The phase offset is per puddle and costs no extra entries -- each streak is painted with a different one of the three reserved indices, so the same rotation shows each of them a different part of the cycle. That is how the technique did it in 1990. The ramp was sky 7-9 until the road was measured against the reference: those three are luminance 107, 115 and 123 against standing water at 50 and mud at 32-40, which would have made the puddles the second-brightest thing in the frame and broken ruling 18b. accent_indigo 2-4 are 44, 61 and 74, and are used essentially nowhere else -- safe only because the sky is drawn flat at step 0 of the same family and never reaches step 2.

hotspots.name: HIS CASE

LOOK_AT.say: My case, still up on the roof, under the driver's hand.
repeat: Everything I own is up there and a stranger is holding it.
He has not dropped it. I have been watching to see whether he would.
Nothing.
The fork against the clasp, faintly, when he shifts it.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is eight feet up and it is not mine to reach for yet.

hotspots.note: Doc 17, state A: on the coach, beats 1–5

hotspots.name: HIS CASE

LOOK_AT.say: My case, in the mud, where it was put.
repeat: Everything I own. It is not heavy and that is the whole difficulty.
My father packed it. He put the fork in first, which tells you what he thought of the rest.
The fork against the clasp. A. It is still four hundred and forty.
Nothing. I have stopped shaking it to hear that, which is a low thing to be caught doing.

overrides.OPEN: A shirt, a razor, three letters, and a tuning fork. I have checked it four times since Sacramento and the contents have been consistent.

hotspots.note: Doc 17, state B: in the mud, from beat 6

there.note:
ON THE GROUND FROM THE FIRST FRAME, beside the coach door, its feet at y800 -- nearer the camera than the coach wheels at 742, so it sorts in front.

SIZED AGAINST THE MAN: a gladstone case is about 22 inches tall, and Thad is 240px for 5'10", so the case is 31% of him -- 89x75. It was 126x128 and read as a trunk.

PICK UP takes it: the case leaves the ground and its CONTENTS enter the inventory. He never carries it around town, which is what Q11 was asking and this answers -- the case is a container, not an item.

hotspots.name: THE WATCHMAN'S LAMP

LOOK_AT.say: A lamp, crossing the road. There is a man behind it and he has not looked at me.
repeat: Still crossing. He is in no hurry and he is not lost.
The only lit thing on this road, and it is going the other way.

LISTEN_TO.say: Footsteps. Even ones. He is counting them.
repeat: Still even.
He has not broken stride once. Not once, in the whole length of the road.

overrides.TALK_TO: He is walking. I shall let him walk.

hotspots.setNote: EVERY RESPONSE HERE WRITES T_HOB_SPOKEN, which is what holds doc 17 beat 9. Hob is a MOVER and not a target -- there is no rect on him and TALK_TO cannot reach him -- so the lamp he carries is the only part of him a player can address, and this hotspot already sits where he now stands. Looking at it or listening to it is speaking to him, and the exchange follows. Added by tools/extract-content.mjs: the lines are the document's, the write is routing.
hotspots.note:
RECT MEASURED FROM HIS STANDING FRAME, not authored. He stands at (600, 720) drawn 230 tall, and the lantern falls at world x626-653 y593-618. It was [480,444,120,168] -- authored for a man CROSSING the road, and when he was moved to stand it missed him by 26px. Nothing would have failed: the hotspot would simply have answered about empty air while the only way to speak to him stopped working.

Q60: this is the only way to address him at all. He is a mover, movers carry no rect, and targetAt never returns one. IF HE MOVES AGAIN THIS MOVES WITH HIM.
hotspots.rectNote: Around the lantern: the flame in his own idle frames is at world x636-643 y612-632 with him at (600, 720) drawn 230 tall, plus 26px of grab. It must clear road_west, which stops at y580 -- lamp_gone especially, because that one is live at the same time as the exit and would otherwise take a click meant for the lamp and start the ending.
hotspots.rectMeasuredNote: Third reading, from the rig rather than from a composed frame: brightest 0.05% of opaque pixels in hob-idle-right/idle-00.png, mapped through rig.figure [632, 1365] at scale 230/1365 about the feet, is world x638-643 y612-624. The rect contains this, the flame reading and the housing reading alike.

hotspots.name: THE WATCHMAN'S LAMP

LOOK_AT.say: The lamp, away up the street. It has not once looked back at me.
repeat: Small now.
Gone round the corner and taken the only light with it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. He has taken the sound with him too.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all.

hotspots.rectNote: Around the lantern: the flame in his own idle frames is at world x636-643 y612-632 with him at (600, 720) drawn 230 tall, plus 26px of grab. It must clear road_west, which stops at y580 -- lamp_gone especially, because that one is live at the same time as the exit and would otherwise take a click meant for the lamp and start the ending.
hotspots.rectMeasuredNote: Third reading, from the rig rather than from a composed frame: brightest 0.05% of opaque pixels in hob-idle-right/idle-00.png, mapped through rig.figure [632, 1365] at scale 230/1365 about the feet, is world x638-643 y612-624. The rect contains this, the flame reading and the housing reading alike.

hotspots.name: THE COACH

LOOK_AT.say: A stage coach, halted, with my case coming down off the back. It has come four hundred miles and it looks it.
repeat: The near wheel has been repaired twice with two different woods.
There is a great deal of dust on it and none of it is from here.

LISTEN_TO.say: The team, shifting. The near axle is dry — it has been dry a long time.
repeat: Still dry. It will be heard from.
Somebody up top is rearranging the load and swearing about it.

overrides.USE: It is going. It is going with some enthusiasm.
overrides.PULL: I have considered running after it. I would like that on the record and nowhere else.

halted.note:
ERRATA 31d, AS RULED UNDER Q20 — THE IMAGE IS GONE AND THE STATE IS NOT. 31d made the coach an object state rather than background art because the shipping background was the DEPARTED composition and this layer was the difference between the two composes: the coach, the team, and the light its lantern throws on the road, which is exactly the set that leaves with it. Errata 53 discarded both composes and the background is now the approved generated plate, so the layer was a picture cut from art that no longer exists, drawn six times magnified over a painting. It is removed. THE COACH IS THEREFORE INVISIBLE THROUGH BEATS 1–6, which is the ruling: honestly absent beats visibly wrong. The state, the gate and every written line stay — the lines are canon under errata 19a and the gate is the mechanism the departure needs, so when the coach is generated against the approved plate, which is doc 42's territory, it drops back in here and nothing else changes.

THE IMAGE IS BACK: art/objects/coach/body-closed.png, the approved coach generated against the approved plate, with the team drawn inside it per errata 31d and both wheels cut out to ride as separate rotating sprites. Door shut, case on the roof rack -- beats 1-2.

unloaded.note: Beat 6 onward: door open, roof rack empty. Set with setState when the case comes down. Verified interchangeable with `halted` -- aligned on the ground line and the rear edge they differ on 13,739px, ALL in the door region: zero in the wheels, zero at the driver, zero across the horses.

hotspots.stateNote:
THE COACH IS DRAWN BY ITS MOVER, NOT BY THIS HOTSPOT. errata 38’s `move` translates a named mover; a hotspot state image is drawn by drawPlate and cannot be translated at all, so the coach had to become an actor to depart. Its record is content/actors/coach.json.

THESE STATES CARRIED IMAGES UNTIL NOW AND THAT MEANT TWO COACHES: this hotspot drew a full-frame layer with the vehicle at x190 while the mover drew it at x1390. Both were correct in isolation and nothing threw, because a state image and a mover are different mechanisms that never look at each other. The states remain because errata 31d’s gating is the mechanism the departure needs, and the written lines are canon under 19a — what is gone is the art.

The layers still exist at art/objects/room-01-coach-halted.png and -unloaded.png. They are what the mover’s frames were cropped from, and Q38 is why the door-open one is unreachable: a mover has clips, not states.

hotspots.name: THE TEAM

LOOK_AT.say: Two horses I can see and I am told there are four more. They have their heads down and they have earned it.
repeat: Nobody has unhitched them. We are not stopping long.
The near one has looked at me twice, which is twice more than the driver.

LISTEN_TO.say: Breathing, and harness. It is the most contented sound on this road.
repeat: Shifting. One of them is bored.
Nothing. They have gone to sleep standing up, which I did not know was available.

hotspots.note: The horses are drawn INSIDE the coach layer (errata 31d): they belong to the same departure and splitting them into a second image would put a seam down the middle of the harness. The team has no image of its own: it is drawn inside the coach body images, which is errata 31d’s reason for generating them together.

LOOK_AT.say: Gone. It made very good time on the way out.
repeat: Not another one for four days. I have checked twice and the answer did not improve.
The ruts are still filling in. That is the whole of my connection to the rest of the world, filling in.

LISTEN_TO.say: The near axle, going away. It will fail on somebody else's stretch.
repeat: Faint now.
Nothing. It is a long way off.

LOOK_AT.say: CONSOLATION — POP. 2,000 AND CLIMBING. The 'and climbing' is in a different hand, and was added later.
repeat: The number has been repainted four times. You can see the smaller ones underneath, each of them once true.
The smallest number underneath is two hundred. Somebody was pleased with two hundred once.

LISTEN_TO.say: It creaks. It would like to be taken down.
repeat: Creaking. It would still like to be taken down.
Nothing. The wind has dropped and it has stopped complaining.

overrides.PULL: It is nailed to a post, in the ground, at the edge of a town. I have been here two minutes and I am already vandalising the place.

lettered.note:
THE PAINT ONLY, NOT THE BOARD. The approved plate already holds the sign; this layer holds what is written on it, extracted as the pixels LIGHTER than the original inside the board face -- paint added on top of bare wood -- so nothing outside the board could drift and the plate itself is untouched.

A lettering layer rather than a regenerated plate, because generation is not reproducible pixel-for-pixel and a fresh plate would risk everything else in an approved picture to change one board.

It reads CONSOLATION / POP. and then four numbers each struck through -- 200, 500, 1000, 1500 -- with 2,000 standing, and AND CLIMBING squeezed in after it in a worse hand. Doc 17’s TOWN SIGN lines describe exactly that and would have been contradicted by lettering it with the town name alone.

LOOK_AT.say: Home is that way. It is eleven hundred miles that way, which robs the gesture of some of its force.
repeat: Eleven hundred miles. I have just come along it and it did not feel optional at the time.
Home is that way. I am not going to keep looking at it.
Nothing coming.
Nothing coming.

overrides.USE: That would be a decision, and I have only just made one.

hotspots.name: THE MUD

LOOK_AT.say: Mud. I have been assured it improves.
repeat: It has come over the top of my boots, which I had not thought possible in the first minute.
Mud. I have been in this territory for ninety seconds and I have formed a view.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Mud is the only honest thing in the territory and it has nothing to say.
repeat: Nothing. It is entirely uninterested.
Nothing. I am going to stop asking it things.

overrides.PICK_UP: I have enough on my boots. I am carrying a quantity of this town already.

hotspots.defaultVerbNote: RULED, AND IT MATCHES ROOM 2. Clicking the ground should walk. This rect is [0, 660, 1920, 204] -- EXACTLY the walkable band Q4 measured -- so with LOOK_AT as the default there was no bare ground left anywhere in the room and no way to move at all: WALK TO is not one of the nine panel verbs, so a click on the floor examined the mud and the player stood still. Measured before the change: a click at (960, 665) resolved to this hotspot and left the walk target where the actor already was. It was invisible before Q4 only because the old band overhung this rect by 84 rows and those rows were bare ground. The three written LOOK lines are untouched and are reached by selecting Look at first, which is how every other examinable thing in the game already works.

exits.name: THE ROAD WEST
exits.rectNote:
THE FULL GAP, x500-650, measured off the plate with a ruler. It was narrowed to x500-590 so it could coexist with the lamp, which left Hob NEITHER BLOCKING NOR CLEAR -- a man in a doorway you walk around. Q63: he blocks it, and clearing him is the way out.

y470-580 IS THE OPENING IN THE FENCE and stops above the lantern, which is the separation that survives him leaving. The gate closes the exit while he is there, so the two are never live together WHILE HE STANDS -- but lamp_gone is live at exactly the same time as the exit, at the lamp's own rect, and it would inherit the collision. Splitting them VERTICALLY is what makes that impossible: the fence opening is what you walk through and the lantern hangs below it, and no sideways nudge is honest because they share a column.
exits.walkToNote: AN EXIT IS WALKED TO AND THEN TAKEN. Clicking it used to put him in Main Street from wherever he stood -- Q12, reported from a play-through as arriving instantly from the bottom-left corner. The engine already does this: `beginInteraction` walks, waits, faces and only then applies, for any target that declares a walkTo. It needed the position, not a mechanism. y710 is just inside the band's new back edge at y700, directly below the gap; `back` because he turns away from the camera to go through it.

LOOK_AT.say: Consolation. There are lamps on in about a third of it.
repeat: Somebody is still awake down there, and somebody is playing a piano badly, and those are two separate facts.
Two hundred yards. It is the shortest part of the journey and I am putting it off.

LISTEN_TO.say: A town, at night, half of it asleep. A piano, flat, some distance off.
repeat: Still flat. Whoever is playing it is not the problem.
Somebody laughing. It is the first cheerful sound I have heard since Sacramento.

exits.note:
THE FULL WIDTH OF THE GAP, x500-650. It was cut to 90 wide to dodge the lamp sideways; that is not the shape of the problem. Hob and the lantern are in the SAME COLUMN of the picture as the way out, so the only honest separation is vertical: the opening in the fence is what you walk through and the lantern hangs below it.

Thad walks through at 575. Q63 gates it on T_HOB_GONE so it is shut while he stands there -- but lamp_gone is live at the same time as the exit, so the geometry has to hold on its own and not lean on the gate. tools/check-exit-collisions.mjs asserts that it does.
exits.endingNote: Doc 17 beat 11. Taking this writes T_THAD_LEAVING and goes nowhere; the beat that flag releases walks him through the gap and travels at its end. setOnTransit exists because doc 14 says transit produces no line -- and a flag write is not a line, which is the same argument stateOnTransit is made from.

atmosphere.note: ERRATA 33b. Declared rather than derived from `horizon`: the sky is measured over these rows and nothing below them may be lighter than its p90. Rows 0-40 are sky and only sky -- the hills start at 42.
atmosphere.skylineNote: The hills and the town downhill -- everything that meets the night sky. NOT the road: a moonlit ground plane in front of the viewer is not seen against the sky, and grading it against one failed twenty thousand pixels for no reason.

lightSources.note: Hob's lamp. The brightest thing in Room 1 at 205 against a night sky p90 of 42.7, and it is SUPPOSED to be -- a source out-blazes a night sky, and errata 33a is about to widen that gap by darkening the collar. Declared, not inferred: a brightness test would excuse the Company facade too.
The coach lantern, dimmer on purpose -- doc 17 allows one bright warm point on this road and Hob has it.
The town downhill, west: lit windows and nothing else. Doc 17's road west LOOK line is 'There are lamps on in about a third of it.'

foregroundNote: NO NEAR PLANE, AS RULED UNDER Q20. art/foregrounds/room-01-stage-road.png was ruling 21a's near plane, cut from the composed Room 1, and errata 53 discarded that picture. Unlike the ten backgrounds it does not resolve when the room is regenerated: a foreground is cut FROM a plate rather than produced BY one, so it needs cutting from the approved plate. Until then the room has no plane drawn over the actor, and in the near mud he passes in front of everything instead of behind it.
walkableNote: Q4, MEASURED AGAINST THE APPROVED PLATE AND APPROVED ON SIGHT. What was here was the composed room's geometry multiplied by six, and errata 53 discarded that picture: three full-width bands covering the bottom third of the frame, so the player walked through the fence, the sign and the shack. Measured on art/backgrounds/room-01-stage-road.png, open mud runs from 7% of the row at y=640 to 41% at y=700 and becomes the surface at y=660 — that is the back edge of where a man can stand, and the band runs 660 to 864. THESE ARE EXTENTS, NOT POLYGONS: the room declares no walk boxes, so nothing here makes the fence, the sign or the shack solid. That is polygon work and a judgement about what is solid in this picture.

walkBoxes.note: ONE BOX. The obstructions run from the band's back edge, not from y690. Measured: in rows 660-690 the left corner is 88-91% not-mud and the right is 96-100% -- the water tower's legs and the woodpile -- so the strip that a y690 top edge would have opened contains no ground to lose. The left structure is solid x0-255 and the woodpile x1630-1920, both from y660 to the frame bottom; walkable is the 1374 columns between them.

scaleMode.beyondNote: PROVISIONAL, AND THE ONE NUMBER IN THIS FILE NOBODY HAS RULED ON. THE CURVE NOW COVERS GROUND THE WALKABLE BAND DOES NOT -- that is unusual and it is deliberate: a staged mover may leave the box (errata 38's own case, and doc 17's exit through the fence gap does exactly that), and without a third sample heightIn CLAMPS, so a man walking away up the road holds 222 exactly and never shrinks. Sliding into the distance at full size is worse than extrapolating badly. THREE WAYS OF MEASURING IT DISAGREE BY A FACTOR OF FOUR. Extending the band's own line gives 133 at y400 and barely shrinks him at all. Anchoring on the room's declared horizon of 348 -- where a man's height must reach zero, which is what a horizon means rather than a modelling choice -- gives 98 at y500 from the far sample and 83 from the near one. Measuring the town's lit windows at about four feet gives 17 at y400, but that assumption carries all the weight and the town is on the far side of a rising hill rather than on the band's plane. RULED: 98, the far anchor, and the reasoning is the tiebreak rather than the model. THE BAND'S OWN CURVE IS NOT A TRUE PERSPECTIVE -- project the far anchor through the horizon and it gives 309 at y830 where the near anchor says 263, so the two do not lie on one line and neither extrapolation is 'correct'. The tiebreak is proximity: the far anchor at y694 is adjacent to the ground being extrapolated into, and the near anchor at y830 is 136px further away through a curve already known not to be linear. Extrapolate from the nearer sample. The town also sits on the far side of a rising hill rather than on the band's plane, which makes the perspective approximate whichever anchor is used -- another reason to take the least-extrapolated reading rather than the most-derived. Overrulable by looking, and should be if a render says otherwise.
scaleMode.note: RESCALED WITH ITS SHAPE UNCHANGED. The anchors were 190 and 225 under the 205 figure; the measured height is 240, so the same curve between the same two rows now runs 222 to 263. farY and nearY are the band's own sample rows and did not move -- only the heights did, which is what 'shape unchanged' means. The box governs, not the zone table: boxAt takes precedence, so a curve left at the old numbers would have quietly overridden scaling.json and drawn him short in the one room that has boxes.

backEdgeNote: THE BACK EDGE IS y700 AND WAS y660, RULED after a play-through reported him walking through the furniture. 660 came from where the mud becomes the SURFACE -- what the ground is, not what stands on it -- and the bench, its rail and the crate beneath it have their bases between roughly y630 and y660. So he could stand level with them or sixteen pixels in front, and at 222px tall he was drawn straight over them: standing in front of something and being drawn over it are the same picture when there is no depth between you. y700 clears every base by 40 to 70 pixels and costs 40 rows of a 204-row band, which against a 240px character is nothing -- the depth curve still gives him 224 there. WALK BOXES THAT EXCLUDE THE STANDING FURNITURE ARE MORE CORRECT and can come later without undoing this: this moves one edge and takes no shape away that anything else depends on.
walkBoxesNote: ONE BOX, AND NOTHING NEEDS A CLIP PLANE. The fence, the bench and the sign all have their feet ABOVE y660 -- the band's back edge -- so they sit behind the walkable area and the player always passes in front of them. He can never get level with the fence, so it neither stops him nor occludes him, and the collision-or-occlusion question answers itself. THE FIRST VERSION HAD TWO BOXES AND WAS WRONG, in a way worth keeping: the obstructions were measured as starting at y690, which forced a full-width strip above them, because `inside()` is a CONVEX-QUAD WINDING TEST and a T-shaped walkable region cannot be one quad. That strip handed both corners back and the player walked into the water tower's legs at the frame edge. The error was not the base's position -- it was proposing a shape without checking what the engine's containment test can express.
